concerns.text: T057 mandates 'Research & Specification' to 'Identify a specific, publicly available source' dynamically at task time. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which requires fetching from the 'same canonical source on every run.' The spec/plan must define the canonical source (URL/DOI) upfront, not delegate its discovery to an implementation task.

T006a and T006b are marked uncompleted (`- [ ]`) and effectively 'REJECTED' in the task list, yet T047a and T056 depend on this retry logic to satisfy FR-001 (API failure handling). A task list cannot silently drop a blocking prerequisite required by a Functional Requirement; this creates a semantic gap where FR-001 is unfulfillable.

T012b (fetch Materials Project data) is marked uncompleted. FR-001 explicitly requires downloading from 'Materials Project AND NREL.' A task list that omits the implementation of a mandatory data source violates the requirement to fetch from both specified sources, rendering the merged dataset (T012c) impossible to generate as specified.

T047c_init creates `data/raw/instrument_registry.csv` with 'default TGA instrument data' (e.g., TA Instruments, Mettler Toledo). This introduces a 'silent constitution drift' by hard-coding specific manufacturer models and precision values into the data layer, violating the constraint in T047c ('Do NOT hard-code specific manufacturer models') and the principle of using real, fetched data rather than synthetic defaults for instrumentation metadata.

T013b calculates `sigma` using `precision` from T047c/T052 registry. However, T047c/T052 rely on a local CSV (T047c_init) that contains 'default' data. If the spec requires real instrumentation metadata (as per the 'Measurement Integrity' narrative), deriving uncertainty from a synthetic default registry violates the requirement that T_d uncertainty be based on 'documented precision' of the actual source measurement, not a fallback assumption.
